curriculum.text: use proper formation patterns to write letters

parts.title: Colour each picture that starts with the /m/ sound.
Read these words. Sound them out: /m/ /a/ /p/.
What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children learn that the letter m makes the sound /m/. They practise forming the letter, listening for /m/ at the start of words, and mapping the sounds in a short word. All reading words use only sounds taught so far (a, t, s, i, p, m).

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Say /m/ together (lips together, humming). The keyword is mouse: /m/ /m/ mouse.
2. Model writing M and m on the board, saying the strokes. Children trace, then write.
3. Name each picture together. Children colour only the ones that begin with /m/.
4. Read the bottom words together, blending each one: /m/ /a/ /p/ = map.

parts.title: Answer key
text: Pictures that start with /m/: mouse, moon, milk, mug. (Not: sun, cat.)
Reading words: am, Sam, map, mat — all read by blending the sounds, e.g. /m/ /a/ /p/ = map.

parts.title: Ontario curriculum link (official wording)
text: In plain terms: children match a letter to the sound it makes — here, m to /m/.
A2.2 — use proper formation patterns to write letters.
In plain terms: children form the letter the correct way.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: confusing /m/ and /n/. Stretch the sound and point to closed lips for /m/.
Make it easier: do the picture sort out loud together before colouring.
Make it harder: ask the child to think of one more /m/ word and draw it.
You'll know it worked when: the child writes m correctly and hears /m/ at the start of new words.
